narrative.summary: Niger has no national AI strategy or AI-specific law. Its only binding AI rules are in the 2022 personal data protection law (Law 2022-59), which defines artificial intelligence, requires AI developers and providers to declare their processing, and sets rules on automated decisions and AI transparency, supervised by the data protection authority (HAPDP).

instruments.issuing_authority: National Assembly of Niger (adopted); promulgated by the President of the Republic
instruments.current_status: Signed in Niamey on 16 December 2022 (the law states it is to be published in the Journal Officiel; not yet verified from the official text: the gazette reference). It repeals Law 2017-28 of 3 May 2017 as amended by Law 2019-71 of 24 December 2019 (art. 112). Amended by Law 2023-31 of 4 July 2023 and Ordinances 2024-16 of 26 April 2024 and 2024-29 of 24 June 2024; the HAPDP's consolidated version (April 2026, information document only) shows the AI provisions (arts. 1, 52, 57) unchanged.
instruments.summary: Niger's general data protection law, which sets up the High Authority for the Protection of Personal Data (HAPDP) and the rules for processing personal data by public and private controllers. It defines artificial intelligence and, in art. 57, requires AI developers, manufacturers and service providers to comply with the law and, when operating from Niger, to declare their processing to the HAPDP. Art. 52 bars judicial decisions based on automated personality profiling and administrative or private decisions based solely on automated profiling (with exceptions for explicit consent, contracts or legal authorisation), and requires that the criteria and data used be disclosed at collection when the processing relies on AI.
instruments.ai_governance_relevance: Only national legal text found with explicit AI provisions: definition of AI, declaration duty for AI developers and providers, and automated-decision and AI-transparency rules.
